newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani stocks end up, seen range-bounded.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani stocks end up, seen range-bounded.

text.p: Pakistani stocks ended up on Sunday as a government relief package for the textile industry improved sentiment, but dealers said uncertan political conditions might keep the index range-bounded.
"Lack of clarity on the impact of the package on the synthetic fibre-makers and political uncertainty would hamper the index rise," dealer Dawar Hassan at Global Securities said.

The Karachi Stock Exchange (KSE) 100-share index rose 11.18 points, or 0.76 percent, to end at 1,490.07. Gainers led losers 196 to 83. Turnover fell to 46.29 million shares from 48.02 million in the previous session on Thursday.
Faysal Bank rose 0.65 to 24.40 rupees and Adamjee Insurance 4.0 to 93. Gadoon Textile fell 2.0 to 40, Umer Fabrics 1.75 to 9.0 and Dewan Salman Fibre 1.60 to 32.25.
Cherat Cement rose 1.0 to 22, Hub Power Co 0.70 to 35.85 and Pakistan State Oil 5.0 to 388. PTCL rose 0.30 to 30.40. Fauji Fertilizer fell 1.0 to 76.25 but ICI Pakistan rose 1.0 to 19.
